title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page is a short exercise in homological algebra about adjoint functors and their derived functors, set inside the divided-power de Rham notes.

Set-up. There are two abelian categories, M and M_N. Judging from the indexing, M is probably graded modules over a graded ring S, such as a symmetric or divided-power algebra. M_N is then the 'truncated' category, modules over S in degrees <= N. The functor tau_N: M -> M_N is truncation. It is exact and has a right adjoint phi_N: M_N -> M:
 Hom_M(M, phi_N P) = Hom_{M_N}(tau_N M, P).

First computation (top of page). The components of phi_N tau_N P are
 (phi_N tau_N P)_i = Hom^i_M(S, phi_N tau_N P) = Hom_M(S[-i], phi_N P) = Hom_{M_N}(tau_N(S[-i]), P).
This uses the shift rule tau_N(S[-i]) = (tau_{N-i}S)(-i). The result is Hom^i(tau_{N-i}S, P), so phi_N is a kind of coinduction.

Second computation. tau_N also has a left adjoint i_N, so
 Hom_M(M, phi_N tau_N P) = Hom_{M_N}(tau_N M, tau_N P) = Hom_M(i_N tau_N M, P),
i.e. h_M phi_N tau_N = h_{i_N tau_N M}, where h_M = Hom(M, -). Taking right derived functors gives
 R(h_M phi_N tau_N) = RHom(i_N tau_N M, -).
Because tau_N is exact, R(h_M phi_N tau_N) = R(h_M phi_N) tau_N.

Conclusion. If M is projective, h_M is exact, and one gets
 Hom(M, R^n phi_N(tau_N P)) = Ext^n(tau_N M, P).
The Ext should read Ext^n_M(i_N tau_N M, P), or equivalently Ext^n_{M_N}(tau_N M, tau_N P).

Purpose. The higher derived functors R^n phi_N of the coinduction/truncation adjunction are computed by testing against projectives. This is presumably used to compare cohomology of truncated (level-N) divided-power or graded objects with the untruncated ones.
errors: The final formulas write RHom(tau_N M, -) and Ext^n(tau_N M, P). What was actually derived is RHom_M(i_N tau_N M, -), i.e. Ext^n_M(i_N tau_N M, P). Under adjunction this equals Ext^n_{M_N}(tau_N M, tau_N P), but the stated form is an abuse of notation.

The identity R(h_M phi_N tau_N) = R(h_M phi_N) tau_N needs more than exactness of tau_N. tau_N must also send injectives to (h_M phi_N)-acyclic objects. This holds, for instance, if the left adjoint i_N is exact, since tau_N then preserves injectives, but it is not stated.
In the first computation, Hom_M(S[-i], ...) and Hom^i(tau_{N-i}S, ...) are used somewhat loosely: the indices and twists are only sketched.

ideas.what: Truncation functor tau_N with a left adjoint i_N and a right adjoint phi_N (induction/coinduction), and the formula (phi_N tau_N P)_i = Hom^i(tau_{N-i}S, P)
ideas.modern_name: Induction/coinduction adjoint triple for restriction along a graded ring map or truncation

ideas.what: Computing the derived functors of a right adjoint by testing against projectives: Hom(M, R^n phi(Q)) = Ext^n(left adjoint of M, Q)
ideas.modern_name: Derived adjunction / Grothendieck spectral sequence in its degenerate case
ideas.where_published: Tôhoku paper 'Sur quelques points d'algèbre homologique' (general derived-functor composition)

deep.surprise_reason: This is routine scratch homological algebra (adjunctions and derived functors) with a small notational slip. There is no new construction or connection on the page.
transcription_corrections: The vertical chain under R^*(h_M phi_N)tau_N reads 'R^*tau_N = tau_N car tau_N exact', not just 'R^*tau_N car tau_N exact'.
'h_M phi_N tau_N = h_{i_N tau_N}' should read h_{i_N tau_N M}.
The struck-out top-left factor is phi_N applied to P, with P marked as an object of M_N; 'Hom_M' carries the subscript M.
The final 'Ext' line is boxed in the original, with the condition 'si M projectif ds M' underneath.
